title: Student submission data linkable to other student records
description: The student ID, course, and submission timestamp transmitted in this flow can be linked to other student data (grades, attendance, previous submissions) to create comprehensive student profiles, potentially revealing patterns about academic performance and behavior.
assumptions: System maintains multiple data stores with student information that can be cross-referenced

title: Student directly identifiable from submission data
description: The student ID is explicitly transmitted with each assignment submission, making the student directly identifiable. Combined with course and timestamp information, this creates a clear identity trail for each submission.
assumptions: Student ID is a unique identifier that can be used to identify individual students

title: Assignment data exposed during transmission
description: The work file, student ID, course information, and submission timestamp could be intercepted during transmission if the connection between student and web app is not properly secured (e.g., missing TLS/HTTPS), exposing sensitive academic work and personal identifiers.
assumptions: Data is transmitted over network that could be vulnerable to interception

title: Multiple submissions aggregated to infer student patterns
description: Multiple assignment submissions from the same student can be aggregated over time to infer study patterns, performance trends, time management habits, and potentially sensitive information about the student's academic struggles or strengths.
assumptions: System retains historical submission data that can be analyzed collectively

title: Student unaware of full data processing scope
description: Students may not be fully aware of all the data being collected (work file, student ID, course, timestamp) and how it will be processed, stored, or shared beyond the immediate submission purpose, limiting their ability to make informed privacy decisions.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not comprehensively explain all data processing activities

title: Student identifier transmitted in grading request
description: The flow transmits student ID as part of submission and grading requests. This unique identifier enables identification of individual students, creating privacy risks if the data is intercepted, logged, or accessed by unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Student ID is a unique identifier for the data subject

title: Linkability of student data across systems
description: Student ID in this flow can be used to link submission and grading data with other student records in the system, potentially creating comprehensive profiles of student academic performance and behavior.
assumptions: Student ID is used consistently across multiple system components

title: Non-repudiation of student submissions and grading actions
description: The flow includes student ID and requesting role, creating audit trails that prevent students from denying their submissions or graders from denying their grading actions. In privacy contexts, this inability to deny involvement can be a threat.
assumptions: System maintains logs of submission and grading requests with attribution

title: Unauthorized disclosure of grading data
description: Submission files, file references, and grading information transmitted in this flow could be disclosed to unauthorized parties, potentially exposing student work, grades, or academic performance data.
assumptions: Grading data includes sensitive academic information

title: Direct Identifiability of Students
description: The Assignment Store contains student IDs alongside assignment files, enabling direct identification of individual students. This creates privacy risks if the data store is compromised or accessed by unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Student IDs are unique identifiers that can directly identify individuals

title: Unauthorized Access to Stored Assignment Data
description: Assignment files containing student IDs, course information, and submission times stored in DS1 could be accessed by unauthorized personnel or systems, leading to privacy breaches.
assumptions: Data store has access controls that could be bypassed or misconfigured

title: Potential Unnecessary Data Collection
description: The grading service stores assignment files with student IDs, course, and submission time. If all this data is not strictly necessary for the grading function, it violates the data minimality principle.
assumptions: Some stored fields may exceed what is minimally required for grading purposes
uncertainty_note: Uncertain whether all data fields are strictly necessary without more context on grading requirements

title: Linkability Across Systems
description: Student IDs stored in the Assignment Store can be linked with other data sources (e.g., student records, grade databases) to create comprehensive profiles of individual students.
assumptions: Student IDs are used consistently across multiple systems in the institution

title: Lack of Transparency in Data Storage
description: Students may be unaware that their assignment files, student IDs, and submission times are being stored in the Assignment Store, or how long this data will be retained.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly communicate data storage practices

title: Processing of teacher identity data
description: The Grades Portal Web App processes identified data when the teacher logs in, including their identity, credentials, and course associations. This enables the system to identify which teacher is accessing which submission queue.
assumptions: Teacher authentication requires identity verification

title: Linkability of teacher to review activities
description: The teacher's login and submission queue requests can be linked to create a profile of their review activities, potentially revealing patterns about which courses they teach and when they review submissions.
assumptions: System logs teacher access patterns

title: Disclosure of teacher credentials
description: During the login process, teacher credentials (username/password or tokens) could be disclosed if the transmission is not properly secured or if the system stores credentials insecurely.
assumptions: Credentials are transmitted during login

title: Teacher unawareness of data collection
description: The teacher may not be aware of what data is being collected during login and queue requests, including metadata about their access patterns, timing, and course associations.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not be prominent

title: Linkability of student submissions to identities
description: An attacker intercepting this flow could link student names with their work content and submission times, enabling correlation of submissions across different contexts or time periods.
assumptions: Flow is transmitted over network without adequate encryption or access controls

title: Identifiability of students through submission data
description: Student names are directly transmitted in this flow, making students immediately identifiable if the data is exposed to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Student names are included in the data payload without pseudonymization

title: Unauthorized disclosure of student work and metadata
description: Student submissions, names, and submission times could be disclosed to unauthorized parties if the flow is intercepted or the portal has inadequate access controls.
assumptions: Network transmission or server access could be compromised

title: Data integrity compromise of submission content
description: Student work content or submission times could be altered in transit, potentially affecting grading accuracy or creating false records.
assumptions: Flow lacks integrity verification mechanisms like digital signatures or checksums

title: Linkability of student performance across courses
description: Grade records containing student id, course, and grade enable linking a student's performance across multiple courses, potentially revealing patterns that could be used for profiling or discrimination.
assumptions: Student IDs are consistent across courses and grade records are stored with sufficient granularity

title: Direct identifiability of students and graders
description: Grade records contain direct identifiers (student id, grader id) that can be used to identify specific individuals, creating privacy risks if data is accessed by unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Student and grader IDs are unique identifiers that can be mapped to real identities

title: Unauthorized disclosure of grade records
description: Grade records stored in the database could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through database breaches, insufficient access controls, or insider threats.
assumptions: Database has access control mechanisms that could potentially be bypassed or misconfigured

title: Data aggregation revealing patterns
description: Multiple grade records can be aggregated to reveal patterns about student performance trends, grader bias, or course difficulty that may not be intended to be disclosed.
assumptions: Sufficient grade records exist to enable meaningful aggregation analysis

title: Non-compliance with educational privacy regulations
description: Grade records contain sensitive personal data subject to regulations like FERPA; improper handling could result in regulatory non-compliance.
assumptions: Applicable privacy regulations exist for educational data in the jurisdiction
uncertainty_note: Regulatory requirements may vary by jurisdiction

title: Processing of identified student data
description: The Grades Portal Web App processes personally identifiable student information (grades and feedback) when responding to student requests. This creates identifiability risks as the system handles data directly linked to specific students.
assumptions: Student authentication is required to access grades

title: Unauthorized disclosure of grades
description: Student grades and feedback could be disclosed to unauthorized parties during the request-response flow, either through interception, improper access controls, or system vulnerabilities.
assumptions: Grades are considered sensitive educational records

title: Potential FERPA compliance issues
description: The flow of student grades may not fully comply with educational privacy regulations (e.g., FERPA in the US) if proper access controls, audit logging, or data protection measures are not implemented.
assumptions: Educational institution is subject to privacy regulations for student records

title: Student unawareness of data processing
description: Students may not be fully aware of what additional data is collected or processed when requesting grades (e.g., request timestamps, IP addresses, device information, access patterns).
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly explain all data collection

title: Unauthorized grade disclosure to wrong student
description: If authentication/authorization fails, the portal could display one student's grades to another student, violating privacy of academic records.
assumptions: Portal uses student authentication to determine which grades to display

title: Grade data tampering before display
description: Grades or feedback could be modified in transit or at the process level before being displayed to the student, compromising academic integrity.
assumptions: Grades are retrieved from a data store and processed before display

title: Access pattern profiling
description: The portal could track when and how often students access their grades, creating behavioral profiles that could be linked to other student data.
assumptions: Portal logs access events with timestamps and user identifiers

title: Non-compliance with educational privacy regulations
description: Grade disclosure may not comply with FERPA or similar regulations if proper consent, access controls, or audit trails are not implemented.
assumptions: System operates in jurisdiction with educational privacy laws

title: Unauthorized disclosure of child's grades during transmission
description: When the parent requests their child's grades, the sensitive grade data transmitted from the Grades Portal Web App could be intercepted or disclosed to unauthorized parties during the data flow, especially if encryption is not properly implemented.
assumptions: Data is transmitted over network between parent device and web app

title: Linkability of parent identity to child's academic records
description: The system creates a link between the parent's identity and their child's grades, which could be exploited to build profiles or enable unauthorized correlation of family academic data across multiple children or time periods.
assumptions: Parent-child account linkage is stored and logged by the system

title: Excessive identification data collection during login
description: The parent login process may collect more identifying information than necessary for the grade request, such as device fingerprints, location data, or behavioral patterns that could be used for tracking.
assumptions: Login process collects authentication and session data

title: Parent unaware of data processing during grade request
description: The parent may not be fully aware of what data is being collected, processed, or logged when they request their child's grades, including metadata about the request timing, frequency, and device information.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly explain all data processing activities

title: Aggregation of grade access patterns over time
description: Multiple grade requests by the parent could be aggregated to create behavioral profiles, revealing patterns about when parents check grades, how frequently, and potentially inferring family circumstances or academic concerns.
assumptions: System logs and stores access history for grade requests

title: Direct Identifiers in Account Management
description: Administrator transmits names and email addresses when creating/modifying accounts, enabling direct identification of students and parents.
assumptions: Data is transmitted over network without additional anonymization

title: Linkability of Account Data to Other Personal Information
description: Account creation/modification data (names, emails, parent-child relationships) can be linked to other student/parent data in the system, creating comprehensive profiles.
assumptions: System contains other personal data about the same individuals

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Personal Account Data
description: Names, emails, roles, and parent-child relationships transmitted during account management could be intercepted or accessed by unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Network transmission or storage may be vulnerable to unauthorized access

title: Non-repudiation of Administrator Actions
description: Administrator account creation, modification, and disabling actions may not be properly logged, allowing administrators to deny their actions.
assumptions: Audit logging may be incomplete or absent

title: Unawareness of Data Processing
description: Parents and students may not be aware when their accounts are being created, modified, or disabled, or what data is being processed.
assumptions: Notification mechanisms may not be in place or may be insufficient

title: Non-compliance with Privacy Regulations
description: Processing of personal data (names, emails, relationships) for account management may not comply with applicable regulations (FERPA, GDPR, etc.) if proper consent and safeguards are not in place.
assumptions: Regulatory requirements may not be fully addressed in account management processes

title: Linkability of account records to other data sources
description: Account records and parent-child relationship links written by the grading service could be linked to other data sources (e.g., student records, payment systems, communication logs) to create comprehensive profiles of families and students.
assumptions: Multiple data systems exist that could be correlated with account directory data

title: Identifiability of individuals from account records
description: Account records containing parent-child relationships enable identification of specific individuals and their family structures, which could be used to target or profile specific families.
assumptions: Account records contain sufficient identifying information

title: Unauthorized disclosure of account and relationship data
description: If the Account Directory data store is compromised, account records and parent-child relationship links could be disclosed to unauthorized parties, exposing sensitive family information.
assumptions: Data store has potential security vulnerabilities

title: Data aggregation from multiple sources
description: Account records and parent-child relationships could be aggregated with data from other systems to create detailed profiles of students and families beyond what was originally intended.
assumptions: Multiple data collection points exist across the system

title: Unawareness of data collection scope
description: Parents and students may be unaware that parent-child relationship links are being stored in the account directory, or the extent of how this data is used and retained.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly explain relationship data storage

title: Non-compliance with children's privacy regulations
description: Storing parent-child relationships involving minors may require specific compliance with regulations like COPPA, FERPA, or GDPR that govern children's data processing and parental consent.
assumptions: System serves minors and is subject to applicable privacy regulations
uncertainty_note: Regulatory applicability depends on jurisdiction and user demographics

title: Explicit Data Disclosure to Third-Party Cloud Provider
description: Full grade records, assignments, and account directory containing personal data are explicitly transferred to an external cloud hosting provider. This represents an intentional data disclosure across system boundaries that should be evaluated against the minimality principle - only strictly required personal data should be shared.
assumptions: The cloud hosting provider is a legitimate third-party service with appropriate security measures in place.

title: Increased Identifiability Through Third-Party Data Storage
description: Account directory and grade records sent to the cloud provider contain personally identifiable information (student names, IDs, grades). Storing this data with a third party increases the risk of individuals being identified from the data, especially if the provider experiences a breach or unauthorized access.
assumptions: The account directory contains PII such as student names and identifiers.

title: Unauthorized Access to Data at Cloud Provider
description: Transferring sensitive academic data to a third-party cloud hosting provider introduces risks of unauthorized access by the provider's employees, contractors, or through security breaches at the provider's infrastructure.
assumptions: The cloud provider has internal access controls but insider threats or external breaches remain possible.

title: Student Unawareness of Third-Party Data Processing
description: Students may not be aware that their grade records, assignments, and account information are being transferred to and stored by a third-party cloud hosting provider, limiting their ability to make informed decisions about their data.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly disclose third-party cloud hosting arrangements.

title: Potential Regulatory Non-Compliance for Student Data Transfer
description: Transferring student records to a third-party cloud provider may violate educational privacy regulations (e.g., FERPA in the US, GDPR in EU) if appropriate data processing agreements, security safeguards, or consent mechanisms are not in place.
assumptions: The institution operates under privacy regulations that govern student data handling.
uncertainty_note: Regulatory requirements vary by jurisdiction; specific compliance status depends on institutional policies and agreements.

title: Unauthorized access to grade records
description: Grade records contain sensitive PII (student grades, performance data). If the DataStore is compromised or access controls are insufficient, unauthorized parties could access confidential student grade information.
assumptions: Grade records are stored with appropriate access controls; the flow uses authenticated connections

title: Linkability of grade records across contexts
description: Grade records could be linked with other student data (demographics, attendance, behavioral records) to create comprehensive student profiles beyond what was originally intended.
assumptions: Grade records contain identifiers that could be used for cross-referencing

title: Aggregation of grade data revealing patterns
description: Aggregating grade records across students, courses, or time periods could reveal sensitive patterns (e.g., performance trends, demographic correlations) that compromise individual privacy.
assumptions: Multiple grade records are being accessed and combined for view generation

title: Unawareness of data processing scope
description: Students and parents may not be aware that their grade records are being processed to build multiple views (student, parent, teacher) and how this data is being used.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly explain all data processing activities

title: Potential FERPA/regulatory compliance issues
description: Grade records are protected educational records under FERPA (US) and similar regulations. Improper access, sharing, or processing could violate privacy regulations.
assumptions: System operates in jurisdiction with educational privacy regulations
